subject: Archaeology
title: Lucy: The Fossil That Changed Everything
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Lucy: The Fossil That Changed Everything.

hook.text: In 1974, a team in Ethiopia found 40 percent of a skeleton from 3.2 million years ago. They named her Lucy.

buildup.text: Lucy was an Australopithecus afarensis — three and a half feet tall with a small brain but upright legs.

discovery.text: Her knee and pelvis proved she walked upright. Walking came millions of years before big brains evolved.

twist.text: The team celebrated the find while playing 'Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds.' The Beatles song gave her a name.

climax.text: Lucy showed that human evolution did not start with intelligence. It started with standing up.

punchline.text: We walked before we thought. Lucy proved it with her knees.

quiz.question: What did Lucy's skeleton prove about human evolution?
options: Big brains evolved before upright walking
Upright walking came millions of years before big brains
Early hominins could both walk and swing through trees equally well
